name: Speculative decoding

features: Zero quality change by construction
Supported by vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, and hosted providers

name: EAGLE / EAGLE-2 / EAGLE-3
description: Feature-level autoregressive drafters conditioned on target hidden features; EAGLE-3 moves to direct token prediction.
features: EAGLE-2 adds confidence-driven draft trees
Current state of the art in draft heads
Supported in SGLang and vLLM

name: Medusa / Hydra / Hydra++
description: Extra prediction heads on the target model generate a candidate token tree verified in parallel.
speed_claim: Medusa-2 up to ~3.6x; Hydra++ 2.70x vs autoregressive (2024)
features: Hydra heads condition on prior candidates
Popularized speculative decoding before EAGLE

name: REST
description: Retrieval-based speculation: retrieves likely continuation n-grams from a datastore, no neural draft model.
features: Skips training a draft model entirely

name: Lookahead Decoding
description: Drafter-free parallel decoding: Jacobi iteration over future tokens plus an n-gram pool for verification.
features: No auxiliary model or training required

name: Multi-token prediction (MTP)
description: Auxiliary modules jointly trained with the target predict extra future tokens; doubles as an integrated speculative drafter.
features: Used in DeepSeek-V3; built into Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and MiMo-V2.6

name: PagedAttention
description: Pages the KV cache into non-contiguous fixed-size blocks, cutting fragmentation and enabling much larger batches.
speed_claim: 2-4x throughput over FasterTransformer/Orca at comparable latency (SOSP 2023)
features: Virtual-memory-style KV-cache management
The enabler of efficient continuous batching

name: Continuous / in-flight batching
description: Admits/removes requests at decode-step granularity instead of waiting for whole static batches.
speed_claim: Up to 23x over naive static batching (2023)
features: Replaced static batching everywhere; verify it is actually on
Measured with vLLM by Anyscale

name: Disaggregated prefill/decode (Mooncake)
description: Splits compute-heavy prefill and bandwidth-heavy decode into separate pools; KV cache reused via distributed storage.
speed_claim: 525% throughput in simulations; 75% more production requests for Kimi (2024)
features: Peer-reviewed FAST 2025
SGLang's specialty; also in vLLM Production Stack / llm-d

name: RadixAttention / automatic prefix caching
description: Organizes cached KV prefixes in a radix tree for cross-request reuse with cache-aware scheduling.
features: Shares KV-cache across requests with common prefixes
Cuts TTFT for agentic loops with long system prompts

name: Prompt caching (API-level)
description: Inference APIs persist processed static prompt prefixes across calls, skipping repeated prefill.
speed_claim: Up to 85% lower latency on long prompts; 100K-token book 11.5s->2.4s (2024)
features: Explicit or implicit depending on vendor
The TTFT lever for agentic loops

name: FlashAttention v1/v2/v3
description: Exact tiled attention that never materializes the NxN matrix in HBM; FA3 adds Hopper asynchrony and FP8.
speed_claim: FA3 1.5-2.0x over FA2 on H100 FP16, ~1.2 PFLOP/s FP8 (2024)
features: FA1: 2.4x BERT / 3x GPT-2 attention on A100 (2022)
Table stakes in every modern engine

name: Grouped-Query Attention (GQA)
description: Groups query heads around fewer shared K/V heads: shrinks KV bandwidth/cache while keeping more capacity than MQA.
speed_claim: T5-XXL: GQA-8 0.28s/sample vs MHA 1.51s/sample at near-MHA quality (2023)
features: Standard in Llama 3, Qwen, Mistral families

name: Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA)
description: Caches a low-rank shared KV latent instead of full per-head K/V tensors.
speed_claim: 93.3% smaller KV cache; 5.76x generation throughput (combined with MoE - do not attribute fully to MLA)
features: DeepSeek-V2/V3/V4 lineage
Trades compute for memory - great for long-context throughput

name: Sliding-window attention / rolling KV cache
description: Attends only to a fixed recent window; old KV entries overwritten in a ring buffer (Mistral 7B).
speed_claim: 2x attention speed at 16K; 8x less cache at 32K with W=4096 (2023)
features: Bounds KV-cache growth for long contexts

name: GPTQ
description: Layer-wise one-shot post-training quantization using approximate second-order information; 175B models fit on one GPU.
speed_claim: 3.25x on A100 / 4.5x on A6000 vs FP16 end-to-end (2022)
features: Weight-only 3/4-bit PTQ
The classic LLM quantization baseline

name: AWQ
description: Protects ~1% of salient weight channels (found via activation statistics) with per-channel scaling - no backprop.
speed_claim: TinyChat runtime >3x over HF FP16 on desktop/mobile GPUs (2023)
features: Activation-aware weight quantization

name: Marlin
description: Mixed-precision auto-regressive GEMM kernel: async weight streaming, L2 eviction hints, offline weight reshuffling.
speed_claim: Near-ideal ~4x vs FP16 at batch sizes up to 16-32
features: The fast INT4 path in vLLM

name: GGUF K-quants (llama.cpp)
description: CPU-first C/C++ runtime with blockwise K-quant families (Q4_K_M etc.) for local inference.
features: Enables 7B-70B inference at tens of tok/s on consumer/edge hardware
No universal per-token multiplier from primary sources - generic 'quantization speed' claims unverified

name: SmoothQuant
description: Migrates activation-outlier difficulty into weights via per-channel smoothing, unlocking INT8xINT8.
speed_claim: 1.56x speedup, 2x memory reduction, negligible accuracy loss (2022/2024)
features: W8A8 INT8 inference

name: SqueezeLLM
description: Non-uniform 3/4-bit quantization by weight sensitivity plus sparse full-precision outlier storage.
speed_claim: 2.4x lower latency vs FP16 on A6000 (2023)
features: Sensitivity-based non-uniform quantization

name: KV-cache quantization (KIVI, KVQuant)
description: Low-bit KV caches: KIVI asymmetric 2-bit; KVQuant non-uniform formats with outlier handling for very long contexts.
features: KVQuant: 1M context on a single A100 (throughput multiplier unverified)
Bigger batches = higher throughput

name: KV-cache eviction (H2O, StreamingLLM)
description: Fixed-memory generation: H2O keeps recent + 'heavy hitter' tokens; StreamingLLM keeps attention sinks + rolling window.
speed_claim: StreamingLLM: 22.2x per-token speed over sliding-window recomputation (ICLR 2024)
features: H2O 'up to 29x throughput' unverified from a primary source

name: MoE sparsity (compute-side)
description: Routes each token through a small subset of experts (e.g. 236B total / 21B active in DeepSeek-V2).
features: Standalone MoE speed multiplier unverified - reported figures entangled with MLA/quantization
Fewer active params/token = higher tok/s at a given quality bar

name: Artificial Analysis - Models leaderboard
description: Standardized model output speed (tok/s) alongside quality and cost across models.
features: Live / continuously updated
The de-facto independent speed reference
Nearly every independent figure in this repo traces to it

name: Artificial Analysis - API providers analysis
description: Per-provider TTFT and output tok/s, including same-model comparisons across endpoints.
features: Live / continuous
Median output tok/s + TTFT per model per provider

name: OpenRouter performance statistics
description: Per-provider throughput (tok/s), TTFT/latency and uptime from production traffic.
features: Rolling statistics (~30-min windows)
Independent aggregator

name: OpenBenchmarks Inference
description: Paired provider requests measuring E2E p50/p99, TTFT p50, p50 tok/s, 95%-floor speed, task success, failures.
features: Snapshot cadence; 2026-09-03 run used 600 requests/provider on GLM 5.3 Flash
Repo: https://github.com/openbenchmarks-labs/inference
Open methodology

name: vLLM benchmark suite
description: bench serve/throughput/latency: request throughput, tok/s, TTFT, TPOT, inter-token latency p99.
features: User-run harness, not a leaderboard
Docs: vllm-project/vllm docs/benchmarking/cli.md

name: GuideLLM
description: Load sweeps on OpenAI-compatible endpoints: TTFT/ITL/tok/s and SLO/capacity analysis.
features: Active OSS project
Tool, not a leaderboard

name: MLPerf Inference
description: Standardized closed/open datacenter & edge submissions; LLM metrics in tok/s under latency/accuracy constraints.
features: Versioned releases (v5.0: Apr 2025, 17,457 results from 23 organizations)
Independent consortium; analysis pages can be vendor-authored

name: ML.ENERGY Leaderboard
description: Throughput (tok/s), TPOT, energy/request, batch sizes.
features: Community/academic; reported actively maintained in 2025
Data: https://github.com/ml-energy/leaderboard/tree/master/data/llm_text_generation/chat

name: HF Optimum LLM-Perf Leaderboard
description: Latency, throughput, energy, memory across hardware/model configs.
features: Irregular updates; appears inactive since ~Dec 2024 - stale
Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/optimum-benchmark/llm-perf-leaderboard

name: LLMPerf leaderboard
description: Output throughput and TTFT under reproducible request-length/concurrency settings.
features: Historical / archived
Harness: https://github.com/ray-project/llmperf

name: H100 / H200 (Hopper)
description: Industry inference baseline; FP8 Transformer Engine; H200 adds 141GB HBM3e.
speed_claim: 33,072 server tok/s on Llama 2 70B (8x H200, MLPerf v5.0)
features: MLPerf Inference v5.0: 34,988 offline tok/s too
The baseline everything else is compared against

name: B200 / GB200 NVL72 (Blackwell)
description: 192GB HBM3e/GPU, FP4 support, NVL72 rack-scale; TensorRT-LLM with in-flight batching and MTP speculation.
speed_claim: 98,443 server tok/s on Llama 2 70B (8x B200): 3.0x over H200 (MLPerf v5.0)
features: TensorRT-LLM claims Llama 4 at >40,000 tok/s on B200 (vendor-published)
DeepSeek-R1 world records claimed (vendor-published)

name: Groq LPU
description: Deterministic SRAM-only dataflow (no HBM), compiler-scheduled - built for low-latency decode.
features: GroqCloud: the fastest GPU-alternative baseline before Cerebras pulled ahead
NVIDIA licensed Groq's chip technology for ~$20B (Dec 2025, reported, secondary source)

name: Groq 3 LPX
description: Vera Rubin-platform decode accelerator: 256 LP30 LPUs/rack, ~500MB SRAM/chip, no HBM.
speed_claim: 3,400 tok/s on Gemma 4 31B at 100K context (AA, Aug 2026)
features: Prefill on Rubin GPUs, decode on LPUs
NVIDIA's '4x vs competing platforms' is vendor-published (competitor unnamed)

name: WSE-3 / CS-3
description: Whole-wafer die: 4T transistors, 900K cores, 44GB on-chip SRAM, 21 PB/s - weights stay on-wafer.
speed_claim: 2,522 tok/s Llama 4 Maverick per user (vendor); 969 tok/s Llama 3.1 405B (AA)
features: Vendor Llama 4 figure vs NVIDIA DGX B200's 1,038 - differing test conditions, directional
No HBM trips = extreme memory bandwidth for decode

name: SN40L RDU
description: Reconfigurable dataflow with 3-tier memory (SRAM+HBM+DRAM) for very large models.
features: '3x speed, 5x efficiency of latest GPUs' (vendor)
Full 16-bit precision at speed

name: TPU v6 Trillium
description: Inference-tuned TPU generation (JAX + native PyTorch/TorchTPU).
speed_claim: 800 tok/s on Llama 2 70B (MLPerf, via The Next Platform, Sep 2025)
features: Secondary source - directional

name: TPU v7 Ironwood
description: 192GB HBM/chip, 64MB software-managed VMEM per TensorCore enabling cross-layer weight prefetch.
speed_claim: Kimi K3: 709 tok/s on 16 TPU v7 vs 452 on 16 GB200, same vLLM engine (Sep 2026)
features: 57% gap published by Inferact (vLLM founding team startup); not independently reproduced

name: Inferentia2 / Trainium2
description: Cloud-native inference silicon via Neuron SDK (NxD Inference, speculative decoding).
speed_claim: Llama-3-70B median per-token latency 21.4ms, ~47 tok/s (AWS blog)
features: Trainium2 is the actively developed line
Third-party '35-45 tok/s' figures unverified

name: Gaudi 3
description: 64 TPCs + 8 MMEs, 128GB HBM2e (3.7 TB/s), FP8, Ethernet scale-out; vLLM backend.
speed_claim: 2x H100 throughput on LLaMA 2 70B at large batch (Intel, 2024)
features: 30% over H200 on 7B/70B/Falcon-180B claimed (vendor, 2024 - take with salt)

name: Instinct MI300X / MI325X
description: 192GB HBM3 / 256GB HBM3e, 5.3 TB/s; ROCm + vLLM with expert parallelism for MoE.
speed_claim: DeepSeek-R1 decode >21,000 tok/s on 8x MI300X (Moreh, AMD partner)
features: AMD ROCm docs: ~12.4k tok/s/node with EP16 on MI300X (vendor)
Independent paper (2026): Kimi-K2.5 (1T-param MoE) at 7,327 tok/s on 4x MI325X

name: Corsair (d-Matrix)
description: Digital in-memory compute (DIMC): logic embedded in SRAM bit cells, no HBM, PCIe Gen5 cards.
speed_claim: 60,000 tok/s Llama 3 8B per server; 30,000 tok/s Llama 3 70B per rack (2025)
features: Inference without GPU or HBM
Deployed via Parasail for decode

name: speedAI240 Slim
description: At-memory compute, 1400+ RISC-V cores, 75W PCIe card - efficiency-first edge/datacenter inference.
speed_claim: 3x the queries/sec/watt of 8x NVIDIA H200 (MLPerf ResNet-50, 2024)
features: Independent benchmark, vendor-submitted; pre-LLM-era workload

name: ACF SuperNIC / EMFASYS
description: Converged 3.2 Tbps Ethernet fabric + CXL memory pooling: offloads KV-cache/prefill memory from GPU HBM.
speed_claim: Up to 50% lower cost per token (2025-2026)
features: NVIDIA license-plus-acquihire reported (single secondary source - unverified)

name: Sohu
description: Transformer-only ASIC: attention wired into silicon, no general-purpose cores (TSMC N4P).
speed_claim: 500,000 tok/s on Llama 70B claimed; first racks shipped summer 2026
features: $800M raised, $1B contracts (reported)
Independent verification pending

name: Asimov
description: Inference ASIC on commodity LPDDR5X (288GB-2.3TB/chip) instead of HBM - capacity over peak bandwidth.
features: Atlas (FPGA gen) deployed at OCI (vendor-published)
$875M raised Sept 2026 (reported)

name: RNGD
description: Tensor Contraction Processor (TCP), TSMC 5nm, 48GB HBM3 (1.5 TB/s), 180W - multi-instance virtualization.
features: 60 users @ 40 tok/s per server
LG AI Research production perf/watt validation (customer/third-party)

name: Napier
description: Logarithmic number system (exponent-stored arithmetic) rack-scale inference hardware.
speed_claim: 1,300 tok/s per user at <1/10th the power of comparable NVIDIA hardware (2026)
features: Via secondary report - treat as directional
